revisionDesc.change: Vote - AcceptText - As most corrections can be accepted here (l. 22 without any doubts), I would in this case also accept ἀ]σ̣θενίᾳ immediately. I agree with Gonis regarding l. 5. In line 9 please correct ἐὰν̣ [ἔχηι]ς > ἐὰν̣ ὃ [ἔχηι]ς, correct in BGU (inadvertence of DDBDP).

Vote - AcceptText - lin5 We can simply retain ὑπὸ τ[οῦ] ἱερέος (BL 13.27). || lin7 [ἀ]σ̣θενίᾳ is better than [Ἀ]λ̣θένια (BL 13.27) || lin22 Δομιττιανο(ῦ) looks good. || Replace bgu 3 p.6 with BL 1.71.
Vote - ReturnToSender - l. 5 is a promising reading, but I suggest publishing with enhanced image and discussion of syntax of [ἀ]σ̣θενίᾳ
Submit - Integration of BL corrections and two further corrections.

Commit - I've integrated BL 13 corrections (based on Olsson, Papyrusbriefe). In l. 5 I went a step further, where after some image processing (Hierax software), one can see the traces of all the letters (τοῦ ἱ). In line 7, Schubart was his second alternative. The word is [ἀ]σ̣θενίᾳ but in the dative I believe (the nominative doesn't make sense but an expression like κατεχόμενον ἀσθενείᾳ et sim.), also in conjunction with him being ἀσθενοῦντι in line 12. In line 22, Δομιττιανο(ῦ) is written with two taus (common by-form) and the abbreviation begins with a raised omicron.
